people.name: Ian Goodenough
people.evidence: House Hansard, 11 Feb 2025, Statements by Members, Ian Goodenough (OPAX corpus speech 1194235; the url is OpenAustralia's index for that sitting day, as OpenAustralia refused the speech lookup on 13 Nov 2026): "After 30 years with the Liberal Party, political circumstances ... caused me to move to the crossbench at the start of this year". The Handbook (PHID 74046) gives one undated Liberal record and no date for the move. The release's 31 Dec 2024 end is a year-end placeholder; his own statement puts the move at the start of 2025, after the last 2024 sitting (28 Nov) and before the first 2025 sitting (4 Feb), so every 2024 sitting is Liberal. The boundary is restated at 1 Jan 2025; no sitting falls on the day this moves.

people.name: Barnaby Joyce
people.evidence: Parliamentary Handbook records of service (PHID E5D): senator for Queensland 1 Jul 2005 to 8 Aug 2013, resigned to contest New England (ROSTypeID 9); his only party record is The Nationals (ROSTypeID 11, undated). His move to One Nation came in his House service (electorate release: from 20 Jan 2026). OpenAustralia's Senate Hansard heads his speeches National Party from 2006 to 2009 and Leader of The Nationals in the Senate from 2010 to 2013.

people.name: Fatima Payman
people.evidence: Wikidata Q112152550, member of political party (P102), fetched 13 Nov 2026: Australian Labor Party to July 2024 and independent from July 2024, both to the month only; Senate term from 1 Jul 2022 (P39). The Parliamentary Handbook (PHID 300707) gives one undated Labor record. Senate Hansard in the OPAX corpus (OpenAustralia) heads her speeches Australian Labor Party from 7 Feb to 30 Mar 2023 (last: speech 829730), Independent from 10 Feb to 26 Mar 2025 (speeches 1194181 to 1194942) and Australia's Voice from 22 Jul 2025 (speech 1195102) to 17 Sep 2026 (speech 1319678). The corpus agrees with Wikidata and dates Australia's Voice, which Wikidata does not list; the corpus is taken. Neither source gives the day in July 2024, so July 2024 is left out; she voted in no Senate division between 27 Jun and 13 Aug 2024 (OPAX division pages), so no division row falls in that gap. No Senate sat between 26 Mar and 22 Jul 2025. The last period ends the day after her latest heading in the corpus.

people.name: Dorinda Cox
people.evidence: Wikidata Q108441696, fetched 13 Nov 2026: one undated member of political party (P102) claim, Australian Greens, and a Senate term from 14 Sep 2021 (P39) in the Greens' parliamentary group; no date for her move to Labor. The Parliamentary Handbook (PHID 296215) gives one undated Greens record. Senate Hansard in the OPAX corpus (OpenAustralia) heads her speeches Australian Greens from 7 Feb 2023 (speech 827091) to 26 Mar 2025 (speech 1194951) and Australian Labor Party from 24 Jul 2025 (speech 1195345) to 19 Aug 2026 (speech 1205733). The change falls between those two headings and no source we hold dates it, so neither period reaches into the gap: Greens from the start of her Senate term to the day after her last Greens heading, Labor from her first Labor heading to the day after her latest. The Senate did not sit between 26 Mar and 22 Jul 2025; divisions on 22 and 23 Jul 2025 keep the source label, marked unchecked.

people.name: Gerard Rennick
people.evidence: Wikidata Q64730677, fetched 13 Nov 2026: one undated member of political party (P102) claim, Gerard Rennick People First, and a Senate term from 1 Jul 2019 to 30 Jun 2025 (P39) in the Liberal-National Coalition parliamentary group; no date for leaving the Liberal National Party. The Parliamentary Handbook (PHID 283596) gives one undated Liberal record. Senate Hansard in the OPAX corpus (OpenAustralia) heads his speeches Liberal Party from 7 Feb 2023 (speech 827154) to 9 May 2023 (speech 829907) and Independent from 10 Feb 2025 (speech 1194180) to 26 Mar 2025 (speech 1194949). The corpus holds no Senate Hansard from June 2023 to January 2025, so his move is undated: Liberal runs from the start of his term to the day after his last Liberal heading, and the divisions between 10 May 2023 and 9 Feb 2025 keep the source label, marked unchecked. Where Wikidata's undated party and the corpus differ for 2025, the corpus heading (Independent) is taken.
